project.name: Summer TCK Negative Fixtures
project.description:
Intentionally-broken beans for sad-path TCK tests (circular dependency, missing dependency, ambiguous resolution, self-injection). These are reached ONLY by the narrow @SummerTest(classes=...) path, which indexes their .class bytes directly via NarrowIndexBuilder (Quarkus ArcTestContainer beanClasses(...) model).
This module deliberately does NOT declare the jandex-maven-plugin, so it produces no jandex.idx. The compiled .class files still ship in the jar and are on the test classpath (so NarrowIndexBuilder can read them). They are invisible to the whole-universe @SummerTest container because that container indexes exactly the running test class's OWN test-classes directory (Quarkus @QuarkusTest model, via TestClassIndexer) -- a separate module's test-classes are simply not on that path. No exclude list is needed: the boundary is the (absence of an) archive on the indexed path, not an allow/deny pattern.
The "no jandex.idx" choice is the explicit, defensive half of that boundary -- even though the test-classes path already excludes this module, producing no index removes any chance of these broken beans surfacing as a whole-universe archive. Do NOT add the jandex-maven-plugin here: a scanned @Component in this module would be discovered and rejected by every normal TCK, not just the sad-path ones.
Package note: fixtures live under com.github.dropguard.summer.tck.negative.fixtures.* so the package prefix mirrors the module name (summer-tck-negative-fixtures). This keeps "which module owns this fixture" readable from the import alone -- the positive fixtures in summer-tck-fixtures use com.github.dropguard.summer.tck.fixtures.*, so the two modules no longer share a package prefix.
